newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Friday:

Spokesman Gerry Kiely briefed on the Farm Council beginning next Tuesday and possibly Wednesday. He said the main points on the agenda were the ban on specific BSE risk material from the foodchain, the farm aspects of Agenda 2000 and the setaside rate.
Spokesmen Josep Coll i Carbo and Nikolaus van der Pas briefed on Tuesday's General Affairs Council.

In answer to a question, Kiely said no country could say it did not have scrapie or BSE. He also said that in this case also the same rules had to be applied throughout the internal market despite differences in the level of risk between countries.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/666: EU requests WTO consultations on Indian import restrictions.
- IP/97/667: Round-the-world skate against racism sets off today from London.
- IP/97/668: Life II programme: the European Commission co-finances 188 new projects for the protection of the environment in 1997.
- IP/97/669: EU structural funds: Commission withdraws global grant for Italian small and medium sized enterprises.
- Eurostat news release No 52/97: EU industrial production up 1.1%.
